title: Chapter 3.  Formation as a Union Territory

blocks.content: Lakshadweep's post-Independence administrative history is comparatively straightforward — a single, stable UT since 1956, with its most significant naming/identity change occurring in 1973 — making this an efficient, high-yield chapter of precise dates and terminology.
From Laccadive, Minicoy and Amindivi Islands to 'Lakshadweep'

Upon Independence and subsequent post-Partition administrative reorganisation, the islands were initially administered as part of Madras State (and briefly saw some administrative division between different mainland units) before being constituted as a separate, centrally administered territory.

The States Reorganisation Act, 1956 formally created the islands as a single, unified Union Territory named 'Laccadive, Minicoy and Amindivi Islands', bringing together the three island groupings (Chapter 1) under one unified administration for the first time, separate from any mainland state.

In 1973, the Union Territory was formally renamed 'Lakshadweep' (meaning 'a hundred thousand islands' in Sanskrit/Malayalam, a poetic rather than literal numerical description) under the Laccadive, Minicoy and Amindivi Islands (Alteration of Name) Act, 1973 — the name by which the territory has been known ever since.

cells: 1 November 1956, under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, as 'Laccadive, Minicoy and Amindivi Islands'
1973, to 'Lakshadweep', under the Laccadive, Minicoy and Amindivi Islands (Alteration of Name) Act, 1973
'A hundred thousand islands' (Sanskrit/Malayalam) — a traditional, poetic name rather than a literal island count
U.R. Panicker (took office 1 November 1956, served only 7 days)

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Lakshadweep's UT formation date (1 November 1956) and its 1973 renaming are two separate, distinct dates frequently tested together — do not confuse the year the UT was FORMED (1956, under its earlier name) with the year it was RENAMED 'Lakshadweep' (1973).

items: UT formed 1 November 1956 (States Reorganisation Act, 1956) as 'Laccadive, Minicoy and Amindivi Islands'.
Renamed 'Lakshadweep' in 1973, under the Laccadive, Minicoy and Amindivi Islands (Alteration of Name) Act, 1973.
'Lakshadweep' means 'a hundred thousand islands' in Sanskrit/Malayalam — a poetic, not literal, name.
First Administrator: U.R. Panicker (7 days in office, 1956).
